{"id": "689f7353-d186-4e5b-948b-a32b94687547", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_dHAFjxjbpsiqLiS2nWeo3L", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/kubernetes-versions.html\",\"content\":\"Table of Contents:\\n- Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle on EKS (char 157-16503)\\n  - Available versions on standard support (char 1790-2078)\\n  - Available versions on extended support (char 2079-2358)\\n  - Version rollback (char 2359-2802)\\n  - Amazon EKS Kubernetes release calendar (char 2803-4261)\\n  - Get version information with AWS CLI (char 4262-6114)\\n    - To retrieve information about available Kubernetes versions on EKS using the AWS CLI (char 4433-6114)\\n  - Amazon EKS version FAQs (char 6115-10806)\\n  - Amazon EKS extended support FAQs (char 10807-16503)\\n\\n**Help improve this page**\\n\\nTo contribute to this user guide, choose the **Edit this page on GitHub** link that is located in the right pane of every page.\\n\\n# Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle on EKS\\n\\n**Tip:**\\n\\nRegister for upcoming Amazon EKS workshops.\\n\\nKubernetes rapidly evolves with new features, design updates, and bug fixes. The community releases new Kubernetes minor versions (such as `1.37`) on average once every four months. Amazon EKS follows the upstream release and deprecation cycle for minor versions. As new Kubernetes versions become available in Amazon EKS, we recommend that you proactively update your clusters to use the latest available version.\\n\\nA minor version is under standard support in Amazon EKS for the first 14 months after it\u2019s released. Once a version is past the end of standard support date, it enters extended support for the next 12 months. Extended support allows you to stay at a specific Kubernetes version for longer at an additional cost per cluster hour. If you haven\u2019t updated your cluster before the extended support period ends, your cluster is auto-upgraded to the oldest currently supported extended version.\\n\\nExtended support is enabled by default. To disable, see Disable EKS extended support.\\n\\nWe recommend that you create your cluster with the latest available Kubernetes version supported by Amazon EKS. If your application requires a specific version of Kubernetes, you can select older versions. You can create new Amazon EKS clusters on any version offered in standard or extended support.\\n\\n**Nitro Sandboxes version support:**\\n\\nNitro Sandboxes requires Kubernetes version 1.36 or later. It is supported on the two latest versions. For more information, see Sandboxing on Amazon EKS with isolated and confidential pods.\\n\\n## Available versions on standard support\\n\\nThe following Kubernetes versions are currently available in Amazon EKS standard support:\\n\\n* `1.37`\\n* `1.36`\\n* `1.35`\\n* `1.34`\\n\\nFor important changes to be aware of for each version in standard support, see Kubernetes versions standard support.\\n\\n## Available versions on extended support\\n\\nThe following Kubernetes versions are currently available in Amazon EKS extended support:\\n\\n* `1.33`\\n* `1.32`\\n* `1.31`\\n\\nFor important changes to be aware of for each version in extended support, see Kubernetes versions extended support.\\n\\n## Version rollback\\n\\nClusters upgraded through in-place upgrade can be rolled back to the previous minor version within 7 days of the upgrade completing. To roll back to a version in extended support, you must first change the cluster\u2019s upgrade policy to `EXTENDED`. Clusters that were automatically upgraded at the end of extended support cannot be rolled back. For more information, see Roll back a cluster to a previous Kubernetes version.\\n\\n## Amazon EKS Kubernetes release calendar\\n\\nThe following table shows important release and support dates to consider for each Kubernetes version. Billing for extended support starts at the beginning of the day that the version reaches end of standard support, in the UTC+0 timezone. The dates in the following table use the UTC+0 timezone.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nDates with only a month and a year are approximate and are updated with an exact date when it\u2019s known.\\n\\nTo receive notifications of all source file changes to this specific documentation page, you can subscribe to the following URL with an RSS reader:\\n\\n```\\nhttps://github.com/awsdocs/amazon-eks-user-guide/commits/mainline/latest/ug/versioning/kubernetes-versions.adoc.atom\\n```\\n\\n| Kubernetes version | Upstream release | Amazon EKS release | End of standard support | End of extended support |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `1.37` | August 26, 2026 | October 1, 2026 | December 1, 2027 | December 1, 2028 |\\n| `1.36` | April 22, 2026 | June 2, 2026 | August 2, 2027 | August 2, 2028 |\\n| `1.35` | December 17, 2025 | January 27, 2026 | March 27, 2027 | March 27, 2028 |\\n| `1.34` | August 27, 2025 | October 2, 2025 | December 2, 2026 | December 2, 2027 |\\n| `1.33` | April 23, 2025 | May 29, 2025 | July 29, 2026 | July 29, 2027 |\\n| `1.32` | December 11, 2024 | January 23, 2025 | March 23, 2026 | March 23, 2027 |\\n| `1.31` | August 13, 2024 | September 26, 2024 | November 26, 2025 | November 26, 2026 |\\n\\n## Get version information with AWS CLI\\n\\nYou can use the AWS CLI to get information about Kubernetes versions available on EKS, such as the end date of Standard Support.\\n\\n### To retrieve information about available Kubernetes versions on EKS using the AWS CLI\\n\\n1. Open your terminal.\\n2. Ensure you have the AWS CLI installed and configured. For more information, see Installing or updating to the latest version of the CLI.\\n3. Run the following command:\\n\\n   ```\\n   aws eks describe-cluster-versions\\n   ```\\n4. The command will return a JSON output with details about the available cluster versions. Here\u2019s an example of the output:\\n\\n   ```\\n   {\\n       \\\"clusterVersions\\\": [\\n           {\\n               \\\"clusterVersion\\\": \\\"1.31\\\",\\n               \\\"clusterType\\\": \\\"eks\\\",\\n               \\\"defaultPlatformVersion\\\": \\\"eks.21\\\",\\n               \\\"defaultVersion\\\": true,\\n               \\\"releaseDate\\\": \\\"2024-09-25T17:00:00-07:00\\\",\\n               \\\"endOfStandardSupportDate\\\": \\\"2025-11-25T16:00:00-08:00\\\",\\n               \\\"endOfExtendedSupportDate\\\": \\\"2026-11-25T16:00:00-08:00\\\",\\n               \\\"status\\\": \\\"STANDARD_SUPPORT\\\",\\n               \\\"kubernetesPatchVersion\\\": \\\"1.31.3\\\"\\n           }\\n       ]\\n   }\\n   ```\\n\\n**The output provides the following information for each cluster version:**\\n\\n* `clusterVersion`: The Kubernetes version of the EKS cluster\\n* `clusterType`: The type of cluster (e.g., \\\"eks\\\")\\n* `defaultPlatformVersion`: The default EKS platform version\\n* `defaultVersion`: Whether this is the default version\\n* `releaseDate`: The date when this version was released\\n* `endOfStandardSupportDate`: The date when standard support ends\\n* `endOfExtendedSupportDate`: The date when extended support ends\\n* `status`: The current support status of the version, such as `STANDARD_SUPPORT` or `EXTENDED_SUPPORT`\\n* `kubernetesPatchVersion`: The specific Kubernetes patch version\\n\\n## Amazon EKS version FAQs\\n\\n**How many Kubernetes versions are available in standard support?**\\n:   In line with the Kubernetes community support for Kubernetes versions, Amazon EKS is committed to offering support for at least three Kubernetes versions at any given time. We will announce the end of standard support date of a given Kubernetes minor version at least 60 days in advance. Because of the Amazon EKS qualification and release process for new Kubernetes versions, the end of standard support date of a Kubernetes version on Amazon EKS will be after the date that the Kubernetes project stops supporting the version upstream.\\n\\n**How long does a Kubernetes version receive standard support by Amazon EKS?**\\n:   A Kubernetes version receives standard support for 14 months after first being available on Amazon EKS. This is true even if upstream Kubernetes no longer supports a version that\u2019s available on Amazon EKS. We backport security patches that are applicable to the Kubernetes versions that are supported on Amazon EKS.\\n\\n**Am I notified when standard support is ending for a Kubernetes version on Amazon EKS?**\\n:   Yes. If any clusters in your account are running the version nearing the end of support, Amazon EKS sends out a notice through the AWS Health Dashboard approximately 12 months after the Kubernetes version was released on Amazon EKS. The notice includes the end of support date. This is at least 60 days from the date of the notice.\\n\\n**Which Kubernetes features are supported by Amazon EKS?**\\n:   Amazon EKS supports all generally available (GA) features of the Kubernetes API. New beta APIs aren\u2019t enabled in clusters by default. However, previously existing beta APIs and new versions of existing beta APIs continue to be enabled by default. Alpha features aren\u2019t supported.\\n\\n**Are Amazon EKS managed node groups automatically updated along with the cluster control plane version?**\\n:   No. A managed node group creates Amazon EC2 instances in your account. These instances aren\u2019t automatically upgraded when you or Amazon EKS update your control plane. For more information, see Update a managed node group for your cluster. We recommend maintaining the same Kubernetes version on your control plane and nodes.\\n\\n**Are self-managed node groups automatically updated along with the cluster control plane version?**\\n:   No. A self-managed node group includes Amazon EC2 instances in your account. These instances aren\u2019t automatically upgraded when you or Amazon EKS update the control plane version on your behalf. A self-managed node group doesn\u2019t have any indication in the console that it needs updating. You can view the `kubelet` version installed on a node by selecting the node in the **Nodes** tab of the **Compute** page of your cluster to determine which nodes need updating. You must manually update the nodes. For more information, see Update self-managed nodes for your cluster.\\n\\n    The Kubernetes project tests compatibility between the control plane and nodes for up to three minor versions. For example, `1.34` nodes continue to operate when orchestrated by a `1.37` control plane. However, running a cluster with nodes that are persistently three minor versions behind the control plane isn\u2019t recommended. For more information, see Kubernetes version and version skew support policy in the Kubernetes documentation. We recommend maintaining the same Kubernetes version on your control plane and nodes.\\n\\n**Are Pods running on Fargate automatically upgraded with an automatic cluster control plane version upgrade?**\\n:   No. We strongly recommend running Fargate Pods as part of a replication controller, such as a Kubernetes deployment. Then do a rolling restart of all Fargate Pods. The new version of the Fargate Pod is deployed with a `kubelet` version that\u2019s the same version as your updated cluster control plane version. improve this page**\\\\n\\\\nTo contribute to this user guide, choose the **Edit this page on GitHub** link that is located in the right pane of every page.\\\\n\\\\n# Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle on EKS\\\\n\\\\n**Tip:**\\\\n\\\\nRegister for upcoming Amazon EKS workshops.\\\\n\\\\nKubernetes rapidly evolves with new features, design updates, and bug fixes. The community releases new Kubernetes minor versions (such as `1.37`) on average once every four months. Amazon EKS follows the upstream release and deprecation cycle for minor versions. As new Kubernetes versions become available in Amazon EKS, we recommend that you proactively update your clusters to use the latest available version.\\\\n\\\\nA minor version is under standard support in Amazon EKS for the first 14 months after it\u2019s released. Once a version is past the end of standard support date, it enters extended support for the next 12 months. Extended support allows you to stay at a specific Kubernetes version for longer at an additional cost per cluster hour. If you haven\u2019t updated your cluster before the extended support period ends, your cluster is auto-upgraded to the oldest currently supported extended version.\\\\n\\\\nExtended support is enabled by default. To disable, see Disable EKS extended support.\\\\n\\\\nWe recommend that you create your cluster with the latest available Kubernetes version supported by Amazon EKS. If your application requires a specific version of Kubernetes, you can select older versions. You can create new Amazon EKS clusters on any version offered in standard or extended support.\\\\n\\\\n**Nitro Sandboxes version support:**\\\\n\\\\nNitro Sandboxes requires Kubernetes version 1.36 or later. It is supported on the two latest versions. For more information, see Sandboxing on Amazon EKS with isolated and confidential pods.\\\\n\\\\n## Available versions on standard support\\\\n\\\\nThe following Kubernetes versions are currently available in Amazon EKS standard support:\\\\n\\\\n* `1.37`\\\\n* `1.36`\\\\n* `1.35`\\\\n* `1.34`\\\\n\\\\nFor important changes to be aware of for each version in standard support, see Kubernetes versions standard support.\\\\n\\\\n## Available versions on extended support\\\\n\\\\nThe following Kubernetes versions are currently available in Amazon EKS extended support:\\\\n\\\\n* `1.33`\\\\n* `1.32`\\\\n* `1.31`\\\\n\\\\nFor important changes to be aware of for each version in extended support, see Kubernetes versions extended support.\\\\n\\\\n## Version rollback\\\\n\\\\nClusters upgraded through in-place upgrade can be rolled back to the previous minor version within 7 days of the upgrade completing. To roll back to a version in extended support, you must first change the cluster\u2019s upgrade policy to `EXTENDED`. Clusters that were automatically upgraded at the end of extended support cannot be rolled back. For more information, see Roll back a cluster to a previous Kubernetes version.\\\\n\\\\n## Amazon EKS Kubernetes release calendar\\\\n\\\\nThe following table shows important release and support dates to consider for each Kubernetes version. Billing for extended support starts at the beginning of the day that the version reaches end of standard support, in the UTC+0 timezone. The dates in the following table use the UTC+0 timezone.\\\\n\\\\n**Note:**\\\\n\\\\nDates with only a month and a year are approximate and are updated with an exact date when it\u2019s known.\\\\n\\\\nTo receive notifications of all source file changes to this specific documentation page, you can subscribe to the following URL with an RSS reader:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nhttps://github.com/awsdocs/amazon-eks-user-guide/commits/mainline/latest/ug/versioning/kubernetes-versions.adoc.atom\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n| Kubernetes version | Upstream release | Amazon EKS release | End of standard support | End of extended support |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| `1.37` | August 26, 2026 | October 1, 2026 | December 1, 2027 | December 1, 2028 |\\\\n| `1.36` | April 22, 2026 | June 2, 2026 | August 2, 2027 | August 2, 2028 |\\\\n| `1.35` | December 17, 2025 | January 27, 2026 | March 27, 2027 | March 27, 2028 |\\\\n| `1.34` | August 27, 2025 | October 2, 2025 | December 2, 2026 | December 2, 2027 |\\\\n| `1.33` | April 23, 2025 | May 29, 2025 | July 29, 2026 | July 29, 2027 |\\\\n| `1.32` | December 11, 2024 | January 23, 2025 | March 23, 2026 | March 23, 2027 |\\\\n| `1.31` | August 13, 2024 | September 26, 2024 | November 26, 2025 | November 26, 2026 |\\\\n\\\\n## Get version information with AWS CLI\\\\n\\\\nYou can use the AWS CLI to get information about Kubernetes versions available on EKS, such as the end date of Standard Support.\\\\n\\\\n### To retrieve information about available Kubernetes versions on EKS using the AWS CLI\\\\n\\\\n1. Open your terminal.\\\\n2. Ensure you have the AWS CLI installed and configured. For more information, see Installing or updating to the latest version of the CLI.\\\\n3. Run the following command:\\\\n\\\\n   ```\\\\n   aws eks describe-cluster-versions\\\\n   ```\\\\n4. The command will return a JSON output with details about the available cluster versions. Here\u2019s an example of the output:\\\\n\\\\n   ```\\\\n   {\\\\n       \\\\\"clusterVersions\\\\\": [\\\\n           {\\\\n               \\\\\"clusterVersion\\\\\": \\\\\"1.31\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"clusterType\\\\\": \\\\\"eks\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"defaultPlatformVersion\\\\\": \\\\\"eks.21\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"defaultVersion\\\\\": true,\\\\n               \\\\\"releaseDate\\\\\": \\\\\"2024-09-25T17:00:00-07:00\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"endOfStandardSupportDate\\\\\": \\\\\"2025-11-25T16:00:00-08:00\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"endOfExtendedSupportDate\\\\\": \\\\\"2026-11-25T16:00:00-08:00\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"status\\\\\": \\\\\"STANDARD_SUPPORT\\\\\",\\\\n               \\\\\"kubernetesPatchVersion\\\\\": \\\\\"1.31.3\\\\\"\\\\n           }\\\\n       ]\\\\n   }\\\\n   ```\\\\n\\\\n**The output provides the following information for each cluster version:**\\\\n\\\\n* `clusterVersion`: The Kubernetes version of the EKS cluster\\\\n* `clusterType`: The type of cluster (e.g., \\\\\"eks\\\\\")\\\\n* `defaultPlatformVersion`: The default EKS platform version\\\\n* `defaultVersion`: Whether this is the default version\\\\n* `releaseDate`: The date when this version was released\\\\n* `endOfStandardSupportDate`: The date when standard support ends\\\\n* `endOfExtendedSupportDate`: The date when extended support ends\\\\n* `status`: The current support status of the version, such as `STANDARD_SUPPORT` or `EXTENDED_SUPPORT`\\\\n* `kubernetesPatchVersion`: The specific Kubernetes patch version\\\\n\\\\n## Amazon EKS version FAQs\\\\n\\\\n**How many Kubernetes versions are available in standard support?**\\\\n:   In line with the Kubernetes community support for Kubernetes versions, Amazon EKS is committed to offering support for at least three Kubernetes versions at any given time. We will announce the end of standard support date of a given Kubernetes minor version at least 60 days in advance. Because of the Amazon EKS qualification and release process for new Kubernetes versions, the end of standard support date of a Kubernetes version on Amazon EKS will be after the date that the Kubernetes project stops supporting the version upstream.\\\\n\\\\n**How long does a Kubernetes version receive standard support by Amazon EKS?**\\\\n:   A Kubernetes version receives standard support for 14 months after first being available on Amazon EKS. This is true even if upstream Kubernetes no longer supports a version that\u2019s available on Amazon EKS. We backport security patches that are applicable to the Kubernetes versions that are supported on Amazon EKS.\\\\n\\\\n**Am I notified when standard support is ending for a Kubernetes version on Amazon EKS?**\\\\n:   Yes. If any clusters in your account are running the version nearing the end of support, Amazon EKS sends out a notice through the AWS Health Dashboard approximately 12 months after the Kubernetes version was released on Amazon EKS. The notice includes the end of support date. This is at least 60 days from the date of the notice.\\\\n\\\\n**Which Kubernetes features are supported by Amazon EKS?**\\\\n:   Amazon EKS supports all generally available (GA) features of the Kubernetes API. New beta APIs aren\u2019t enabled in clusters by default. However, previously existing beta APIs and new versions of existing beta APIs continue to be enabled by default. Alpha features aren\u2019t supported.\\\\n\\\\n**Are Amazon EKS managed node groups automatically updated along with the cluster control plane version?**\\\\n:   No. A managed node group creates Amazon EC2 instances in your account. These instances aren\u2019t automatically upgraded when you or Amazon EKS update your control plane. For more information, see Update a managed node group for your cluster. We recommend maintaining the same Kubernetes version on your control plane and nodes.\\\\n\\\\n**Are self-managed node groups automatically updated along with the cluster control plane version?**\\\\n:   No. A self-managed node group includes Amazon EC2 instances in your account. These instances aren\u2019t automatically upgraded when you or Amazon EKS update the control plane version on your behalf. A self-managed node group doesn\u2019t have any indication in the console that it needs updating. You can view the `kubelet` version installed on a node by selecting the node in the **Nodes** tab of the **Compute** page of your cluster to determine which nodes need updating. You must manually update the nodes. For more information, see Update self-managed nodes for your cluster.\\\\n\\\\n    The Kubernetes project tests compatibility between the control plane and nodes for up to three minor versions. For example, `1.34` nodes continue to operate when orchestrated by a `1.37` control plane. However, running a cluster with nodes that are persistently three minor versions behind the control plane isn\u2019t recommended. For more information, see Kubernetes version and version skew support policy in the Kubernetes documentation. We recommend maintaining the same Kubernetes version on your control plane and nodes.\\\\n\\\\n**Are Pods running on Fargate automatically upgraded with an automatic cluster control plane version upgrade?**\\\\n:   No. We strongly recommend running Fargate Pods as part of a replication controller, such as a Kubernetes deployment. Then do a rolling restart of all Fargate Pods. The new version of the Fargate Pod is deployed with a `kubelet` version that\u2019s the same version as your updated cluster control plane version.
